title: Mappings and indentation
summary: Mappings associate unique keys with values; indentation defines nesting.
syntax:
parent:
  child: value
sibling: value
rules: Use spaces for indentation; tabs cannot indent YAML blocks.
Sibling keys use the same indentation. Duplicate keys are errors, not a reliable override mechanism.

title: Block and flow sequences
summary: Sequences retain item order and can contain scalars or mappings.
syntax:
items:
  - first
  - second
compact: [first, second]
rules: A block item begins with a dash followed by whitespace.
Indent mapping fields within an item consistently; flow collections use commas.

title: Scalars and parser versions
summary: Plain scalars may resolve to strings, numbers, booleans or null depending on the schema.
syntax:
enabled: true
count: 3
missing: null
text: "true"
rules: YAML 1.2 treats on/off/yes/no as strings under the core schema; YAML 1.1 may resolve them as booleans.
Quote date-like values, leading-zero identifiers and boolean-looking text when a string is required. CloudFormation uses a YAML 1.1 subset; Compose and Actions apply their own schemas.

title: Quoting and special characters
summary: Single and double quotes protect text from YAML indicators and scalar resolution.
syntax:
single: 'it''s literal'
double: "line one\nline two"
plain: ordinary text
rules: Single quotes escape a quote by doubling it; backslashes are literal.
Double quotes support escapes. Quote text containing colon-space or an ambiguous hash comment.

title: Literal and folded blocks
summary: Block scalars encode multiline text with explicit folding and trailing-newline behavior.
syntax:
literal: |
  first line
  second line
folded: >-
  first line
  second line
rules: The literal style preserves line breaks; folded style usually joins adjacent text lines with spaces.
A minus strips the final newline; plus keeps trailing blank lines. Content must be indented beyond its header.

title: Anchors and aliases
summary: An anchor names a node, and an alias refers to the same node elsewhere in the document.
syntax:
original: &node
  key: value
copy: *node
rules: Define an anchor before using its alias. Aliases are references, not text substitution.
The merge key << is not part of YAML 1.2 core. Compose supports it; consumer support varies. GitHub Actions supports anchors but not merge keys. CloudFormation does not support aliases.

title: Workflow triggers
summary: The on key selects events and optional filters for a workflow.
syntax:
"on":
  push:
    branches: [branch]
  workflow_dispatch:
rules: Workflow files live in .github/workflows and end in .yml or .yaml.
When one event has configuration, write all events as mapping keys with colons. Quote on to preserve it in YAML 1.1 parsers too.

title: Jobs and steps
summary: Jobs choose runners; their steps run in order and can invoke actions or commands.
syntax:
jobs:
  job_id:
    runs-on: runner
    steps:
      - uses: owner/action@ref
      - run: command
rules: Each job has its own runner environment; steps in one job share its workspace.
Use working-directory/defaults deliberately. run uses the selected shell; YAML quoting does not replace shell quoting.

title: Job dependencies
summary: needs defines the prerequisite jobs that must complete before a job runs.
syntax:
jobs:
  later:
    needs: [earlier]
    runs-on: runner
    steps:
      - run: command
rules: Dependent jobs normally require successful prerequisite jobs.
Files do not transfer through needs: publish/download an artifact to move files between runners.

title: Build matrices
summary: A strategy matrix expands one job definition into combinations of input values.
syntax:
strategy:
  fail-fast: false
  matrix:
    version: [value1, value2]
rules: Read an axis through the matrix expression context.
include adds combinations or values; exclude removes combinations. fail-fast controls cancellation after failures.

title: Expressions and conditions
summary: Expressions read contexts and compute values; if gates a job or step.
rules: Expression string literals use single quotes inside the expression.
Pass untrusted event text via environment variables and quote shell expansions; avoid inserting it directly into run scripts.

title: Environment and secrets
summary: Workflow, job and step env maps have different scope; secrets come from GitHub contexts.
syntax:
env:
  LABEL: value
# In a step:
env:
  TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NAME }}
rules: More specific env scopes override broader ones. Never commit secret values in YAML.
Fork pull requests normally do not receive repository secrets. Handle missing secrets explicitly and never print them.

title: Token permissions
summary: permissions restricts the capabilities of the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN.
syntax:
permissions:
  contents: read
# Disable all token permissions:
permissions: {}
rules: Setting individual permissions makes unspecified permissions none.
Grant write access only to the job that needs it. Avoid privileged pull_request_target execution of untrusted code.

title: Dependency caches
summary: Caches reuse downloads across runs; their keys should reflect dependency inputs.
syntax:
- uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: directory
    key: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('lockfile') }}
rules: Use lockfile hashes and operating-system/runtime inputs in keys.
Caches are optimizations, not required outputs or secret storage. Code must work on a cache miss.

title: Artifacts between jobs
summary: Artifacts persist named files from a job for later download or inspection.
syntax:
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: output-name
    path: output-path
rules: Use unique artifact names across matrix jobs; artifact v4 uploads are immutable.
Choose retention and missing-file behavior explicitly. Never upload secrets or credential files.

title: Template parameters
summary: Parameters define typed inputs and optional constraints before resource evaluation.
syntax:
Parameters:
  InputName:
    Type: String
    Default: value
    AllowedValues: [value, other]
rules: Parameter types are CloudFormation types, not YAML node types.
NoEcho masks some displays; it does not protect values placed in Outputs, Metadata or resource identifiers.

title: Resource declarations
summary: Resources maps logical IDs to AWS resource types and their properties.
syntax:
Resources:
  LogicalId:
    Type: AWS::Service::Resource
    Properties:
      Property: value
rules: Logical IDs identify resources within the template; they are not physical names.
CloudFormation supports a YAML 1.1 subset with intrinsic tags, but excludes aliases and hash merges. Linting does not verify account permissions or runtime quotas.

title: References and intrinsic functions
summary: Intrinsic functions compute references and values during stack evaluation.
syntax:
Value: !Ref LogicalId
Arn: !GetAtt LogicalId.Arn
Text: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-suffix"
rules: Ref returns a type-specific value; GetAtt selects a documented resource attribute.
Use long-form nesting when short-form YAML tags cannot be directly nested. Generic YAML parsers need CloudFormation tag support.

title: Conditions and conditional values
summary: Conditions choose resources or property values using parameters and intrinsic comparisons.
syntax:
Conditions:
  IsEnabled: !Equals [!Ref InputName, enabled]
# On a resource:
Condition: IsEnabled
rules: Condition on a resource controls whether the resource is created.
Fn::If selects a property/output branch; AWS::NoValue can remove a property. Conditions cannot reference resource attributes.

title: Outputs and exports
summary: Outputs expose selected values after stack operations; exports share values with other stacks.
syntax:
Outputs:
  OutputName:
    Description: purpose
    Value: !Ref LogicalId
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-name"
rules: Never place secrets in outputs: output values are visible in stack descriptions.
Export names must be unique per account and Region; imports constrain later deletion and modification.

title: Services and ports
summary: Services describe containers; ports publish a container port on the host.
syntax:
services:
  service_name:
    image: repository:tag
    ports:
      - "host:container"
rules: Quote port mappings to prevent unwanted scalar parsing.
A loopback host binding limits access to the local machine. Image tags and exposed ports must match the application.

title: Named volumes and bind mounts
summary: Named volumes persist managed data; bind mounts expose an existing host path.
syntax:
services:
  app:
    volumes:
      - data:/container/path
volumes:
  data:
rules: Declare named volumes at the top level as well as mounting them on services.
Bind mounts depend on the host filesystem; read-only mounts protect source data from container writes.

title: Service networks
summary: Compose creates networks and provides service-name DNS to attached services.
syntax:
services:
  app:
    networks: [private]
networks:
  private:
    internal: true
rules: Services communicate using service names and container ports, not host-published ports.
internal restricts external connectivity; it is not authentication. Services share the default network when none is specified.

title: Environment and interpolation
summary: Compose interpolates dollar expressions before configuring container environment variables.
syntax:
environment:
  KEY: "${HOST_VALUE:-fallback}"
  FLAG: "true"
rules: Quote boolean-like environment values so the service receives strings.
A .env file supplies Compose interpolation; env_file supplies container environment. Escape a dollar as $$ to defer expansion to a container shell.

title: Health checks and startup order
summary: Health checks evaluate a container; depends_on can wait for service_healthy.
syntax:
healthcheck:
  test: [CMD, executable, argument]
  interval: 10s
  timeout: 3s
  retries: 5
rules: A health command must exist in the image. CMD uses arguments directly; CMD-SHELL invokes a shell.
service_healthy gates startup only; clients still need reconnection logic for later outages.

title: Explicit scalar tags
summary: Tags select a node type independently of how its text looks.
syntax:
text: !!str scalar
number: !!int "12"
flag: !!bool true
rules: Generic YAML 1.2, tested with ruamel.yaml 0.18.16 safe loading: standard tags construct native values; unknown application tags are rejected.
Quoting changes implicit resolution but an explicit tag still applies. An invalid !!int value fails construction; !!str is useful for identifiers.
A consumer schema can forbid otherwise valid tags. CloudFormation intrinsic tags belong only in its templates.

title: Document markers and streams
summary: A stream can contain multiple independent documents separated by markers.
syntax:
---
key: value
...
---
other: value
...
rules: YAML 1.2.2 / ruamel.yaml 0.18.16: use load_all for streams; load requires a single document.
--- starts a document and ... ends it. Empty documents load as null. Anchors are scoped to one document and cannot cross markers.
Most workflow and Compose consumers require one document; this is a generic data-stream feature.

references.title: Document markers and streams — official reference

title: Merge-key portability and precedence
summary: Some readers support mapping defaults through the legacy merge-key extension.
syntax:
defaults: &defaults
  key: default
instance:
  <<: *defaults
  key: explicit
rules: Tested with ruamel.yaml 0.18.16 and Compose 5.5.1. << is a YAML 1.1 merge extension, not YAML 1.2 core; require consumer support explicitly.
Explicit mapping keys win over merged keys. Merge is shallow, applies to mappings, and does not concatenate sequences.
GitHub Actions supports anchors/aliases but not merge keys; CloudFormation excludes aliases and hash merges. Use explicit fields in those consumers.

references.title: Merge-key portability and precedence — official reference

title: Parser rejection and recovery
summary: Parsing rejects malformed syntax; safe construction also rejects unknown tags.
syntax:
unique: value
nested:
  child: value
rules: Pinned ruamel.yaml 0.18.16 safe loader uses YAML 1.2 and allow_duplicate_keys=False; do not recover by keeping an arbitrary duplicate.
Repair the source, then create a fresh loader after an error. Tabs cannot indent block nodes; flow sequences must close.
Parsing success is separate from schema validation. Unknown safe-loader tags fail construction; use strings or explicit supported tags.

references.title: Parser rejection and recovery — official reference

title: Reusable workflow inputs and outputs
summary: A called workflow declares typed inputs and exposes outputs from its jobs.
syntax:
"on":
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      label: {type: string, required: true}
    outputs:
      result: {value: "${{ jobs.work.outputs.result }}"}
jobs:
  work: ...
rules: GitHub workflow syntax, validated by actionlint 1.7.12: save the callee directly under .github/workflows and call it at jobs.<id>.uses, not inside steps.
Map step output to job output to workflow output. Caller with values must match declared boolean/number/string types; local calls omit @ref.
Expressions stay literal during offline validation; output production, secret availability and permissions still require a runner.

references.title: Reusable workflow inputs and outputs — official reference

title: Local composite actions
summary: A composite action packages steps, with explicit input-to-environment and output mappings.
syntax:
name: Action
description: Purpose
inputs:
  text: {description: Text, default: value}
outputs:
  text: {description: Result, value: "${{ steps.emit.outputs.text }}"}
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - id: emit
      shell: bash
      run: ...
rules: Action metadata syntax, inspected with actionlint 1.7.12 through a local workflow caller. Save as .github/actions/<name>/action.yml; checkout must precede uses: ./.github/actions/<name>.
Composite run steps require shell. inputs do not automatically become INPUT_* variables; map untrusted text into env before shell expansion.
required: true alone does not enforce presence at runtime. Validate nonempty input in the action when needed. Offline tests check metadata/contracts, not runner execution.

title: Concurrency groups and cancellation
summary: Concurrency groups coordinate workflow or job runs that share a key.
rules: Current workflow syntax checked with actionlint 1.7.12. Use workflow/ref or another scoped group to avoid cancelling unrelated workflows.
With the default single-pending policy used here, a group permits one running and one pending member; a newer pending member replaces the old pending one. Dispatch order is not guaranteed.
cancel-in-progress chooses whether to cancel a running member. Offline linting checks syntax/context, not GitHub scheduler behavior.

Current GitHub also documents queue: max for up to 100 pending members, incompatible with cancel-in-progress: true. These examples use the default policy accepted by pinned actionlint; they do not cover queue: max scheduling.

references.title: Concurrency groups and cancellation — official reference

title: Dependency-aware job conditions
summary: Job conditions combine dependency status and explicit status-check functions.
syntax:
needs: previous
if: ${{ always() && !cancelled() }}
rules: Current workflow syntax / actionlint 1.7.12: jobs with needs normally require successful dependencies unless an explicit status function changes that gate.
Use !cancelled() for work that should survive dependency failure but respect cancellation; always() alone can run on cancellation.
needs exposes direct dependency results and declared outputs. Offline checks preserve expressions and verify references, not service status evaluation.

title: Mappings and FindInMap
summary: Mappings hold two-level lookup tables resolved by FindInMap.
syntax:
Mappings:
  Table:
    Key:
      Field: value
Resources: ...
Outputs:
  Value:
    Value: !FindInMap [Table, Key, Field]
rules: CloudFormation YAML 1.1 subset; cfn-lint 1.57.2 bundled us-east-1 schemas. Classic FindInMap takes mapping name, top key and second key.
Mapping entries are literal strings/lists; use parameters or pseudo-parameters as lookup keys, not arbitrary expressions inside the table.
LanguageExtensions adds enhanced lookup features but is not enabled here. Static linting cannot prove every deployment-time parameter/key combination.

title: Nested resource property structures
summary: Resource schemas distinguish object, list and scalar property shapes.
syntax:
Resources:
  LogicalId:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: name
          Value: text
      RedrivePolicy:
        deadLetterTargetArn: ...
        maxReceiveCount: 5
rules: cfn-lint 1.57.2 validates against bundled us-east-1 schemas; CloudFormation YAML uses its supported YAML 1.1 subset.
Tags is a sequence of Key/Value objects; RedrivePolicy is an object. Indentation can yield valid YAML with an invalid resource property type.
Linting checks static types and references, not account quotas, permissions or whether an external ARN exists.

references.title: Nested resource property structures — official reference

title: Compose intrinsic functions explicitly
summary: Long-form mappings let intrinsic functions nest without ambiguous adjacent tags.
syntax:
Value:
  Fn::Join:
    - delimiter
    - [literal, {Ref: Parameter}]
rules: CloudFormation subset / cfn-lint 1.57.2. A YAML node can have only one tag; use long-form mappings for nested functions when short forms conflict.
Fn::Join requires a delimiter and a list; Fn::Sub accepts a string or a string plus a variable map.
Reference valid parameters/resources or explicitly supply substitution variables. Offline validation cannot evaluate account-specific pseudo-parameters.

references.title: Compose intrinsic functions explicitly — official reference

title: Build configuration without building
summary: A service build section describes a context, Dockerfile and optional build arguments.
syntax:
services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile_inline: |
        FROM image
      args:
        MODE: value
rules: Compose 5.5.1, current Compose Build Specification. config normalizes the definition without building or contacting a daemon.
dockerfile_inline requires Compose 2.17+ and cannot be combined with dockerfile. Paths are relative to the base Compose project directory.
Build arguments are not secrets. Validation does not verify a Dockerfile, image availability or a successful build.

references.title: Build configuration without building — official reference

title: Optional service profiles
summary: Profiles control which optional services participate in a Compose project.
syntax:
services:
  tool:
    image: image
    profiles: [debug]
rules: Compose 5.5.1 / Compose profiles specification: unprofiled services are always enabled; --profile activates matching profiled services.
Explicitly targeting a profiled service auto-enables that service and its dependencies, not every service sharing its profile.
config --profiles lists declared names, not running services. Inspect config with/without a profile; no services need to start.

title: Layered configuration and reset tags
summary: Compose merges files in order, with special handling for unique resources and commands.
syntax:
# Base file supplied first with -f
services:
  app:
    environment:
      MODE: base
# In a separate override file:
# services: {app: {environment: {MODE: local}}}
rules: Compose 5.5.1: files merge in -f order and relative paths use the first file. Mappings merge by key; ports/volumes have uniqueness rules.
!reset removes a value using its default type; !override replaces it without normal merge rules (requires Compose 2.24.4+). These tags are consumer-specific, not safe-loader YAML core.
Entrypoint/command/healthcheck.test replace rather than append. Validate the combined project; a fragment alone can legitimately lack an image.

references.title: Layered configuration and reset tags — official reference
